ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a binary symmetric channel BSC, with input X on the left and output Y on the right. The input side is labeled X=0 and X=1, and the prior probabilities are respectively P[X=0]=0.2 and P[X=1]=0.8. The output side is labeled Y=0 and Y=1. In the figure, the horizontal branches without error are labeled 6/7, that is, P(Y=0|X=0)=6/7 and P(Y=1|X=1)=6/7; the crossed branches are labeled 1/7, that is, P(Y=1|X=0)=1/7 and P(Y=0|X=1)=1/7. Reasoning: What the problem asks for is P(X=1 | Y=0). Receiving Y=0 has two paths: one is that after sending X=1, a crossing occurs, with probability 0.8 × 1/7; the other is that after sending X=0, no error occurs, with probability 0.2 × 6/7. Therefore, by Bayes' formula, P(X=1|Y=0) = (0.8 × 1/7) / [(0.8 × 1/7) + (0.2 × 6/7)] = 0.8 / (0.8 + 1.2) = 0.8 / 2 = 0.4.
